# Security Policy

## Supported versions

Security fixes are made to the latest release, published on the [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/eppokcmemgiphpegpighpfnhpjggpmoc) and the [Firefox Add-ons](https://addons.mozilla.org/firefox/addon/ai-bulk-chat-manager/) site (when the listing is live) and tagged in this repository. Older versions are not patched; please update.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please **do not open a public issue** for a security problem.

Report it privately with GitHub's private vulnerability reporting:

1. Go to the repository's **Security** tab.
2. Choose **Report a vulnerability**.
3. Describe the problem and how to reproduce it.

Direct link: <https://github.com/ehsanenaloo/AI-Bulk-Chat-Manager/security/advisories/new>

Helpful details:

- the extension version (shown at the top of the Options page) and the browser and its version,
- the affected component (toolbar popup, in-page panel, Options page, background worker, export),
- the site it happens on (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Grok),
- clear reproduction steps, ideally on a test account rather than your real chats,
- the impact you believe it has.

Please do not include real chat titles, chat links, session cookies, access tokens or other credentials in a report.

## What to expect

This is a volunteer-maintained project, so response times are best effort. The maintainer will acknowledge a report, assess it, work on a fix for confirmed issues and credit you in the release notes if you wish. Please allow a reasonable time to ship a fix before disclosing the issue publicly.

## Scope

In scope:

- code in this repository that ships in the extension,
- ways to make the extension read, change or leak data beyond what its documented permissions and behavior allow (see [PRIVACY.md](../docs/PRIVACY.md)),
- ways for a web page, or a chat title or link on the page, to make the extension run code, click something it should not, or act on a chat the user did not select,
- cross-site scripting or injection through chat titles, links or translated strings, including the exported files,
- anything that exposes the user's session or access token to a page or another party.

Out of scope:

- issues that require an already compromised browser, operating system or browser profile,
- vulnerabilities in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or in other extensions,
- vulnerabilities in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Grok themselves, which should be reported to their owners,
- findings that depend on a modified copy of the extension,
- social engineering, and the fact that the site's own undocumented endpoints can change or stop working.

## Design notes relevant to security researchers

- Permissions are `activeTab`, `scripting` and `storage`. The Chrome and Edge package has no `host_permissions`; the extension runs on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok through its content script matches only. The Firefox package, generated by `scripts/build-firefox.mjs`, declares those same five sites as host permissions because Firefox asks for them at install.
- There are no `web_accessible_resources`, no externally connectable origins and no custom content security policy.
- The panel lives in a shadow root. Chat titles and links from the page are rendered as text, never as HTML.
- The "fast" path sends same-origin requests from the page to the site's own backend with the user's existing session. The extension has no server and sends nothing to the author or to a third party.
- The background worker only opens `https:` links and only serves the extension's own translation and style files.
